speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of appendicitis is incorrect given the prominent jaundice and agitation; this presentation is highly suggestive of acute liver injury. speaker: Doctor

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte Count: 9,750/mm3, Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%, Platelet Count: 365,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal CBC rules out hemolysis and sepsis, while the previous negative workup excludes viral, autoimmune, and common toxic etiologies. Given the young male patient's acute presentation of jaundice, agitation, and confusion with an otherwise negative standard workup, this clinical picture is classic for Acute Wilson's Disease, where ceruloplasmin can occasionally be normal during acute inflammation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Wilson's Disease
